title: Set audio levels
summary: Raise or lower a clip's volume with Audio Gain and check the meters.

steps.say: Click an empty spot in the Timeline at the bottom right so it has focus.

check.prompt: Is the Timeline panel at the bottom right outlined in blue as the active panel, with clips on it?

hints: The Timeline is the panel with the V1 and A1 track rows. A blue outline shows it is active.
If the Timeline is empty, drag a clip from the Project panel into it first.
steps.why: Premiere sends shortcuts to the panel with focus, so the Timeline must be active.

steps.say: Click the clip whose sound you want to change.

check.prompt: Is a clip highlighted as selected in the Timeline?

hints: Clicking the audio part on an A track selects it, and its video if they are linked.
Select several clips with Shift click to change them together.
steps.why: Audio Gain works on the selected clips.

steps.say: Press G to open Audio Gain.

checks.prompt: Is the Audio Gain window open?

hints: Click the clip first so the Timeline has focus, then press G.
You can also right-click the clip and choose Audio Gain.
steps.why: Audio Gain changes loudness by a number you type, which is precise and repeatable.

steps.say: Choose Adjust Gain by, type a number such as 3 or minus 3, then click OK.

check.prompt: Has the Audio Gain window closed, with the clip waveform taller or shorter than before?

hints: Positive numbers make it louder, negative numbers quieter. The unit is decibels.
Choose Normalize Max Peak to, with minus 3, to set loudness automatically.
steps.why: Small changes of a few decibels are usually all a clip needs.

steps.say: Press Space to play and watch the audio meters at the right of the Timeline.

checks.prompt: Is the video playing with the audio meters moving?

hints: The meters are two narrow bars at the far right. Press Space again to stop.
If you see no meters, open the Window menu and choose Audio Meters.
steps.why: The meters show whether the sound is too quiet or too loud.

steps.say: If the meters touch red at the top, lower the gain a little and play again.
hints: Aim for loud parts peaking a little below zero, around minus 6.
Select the clip, press G, and type a negative number to lower it.
steps.why: Red at the top means distortion, which sounds harsh to viewers.
